## Why do corporate credit cards fall short for Indian teams?


Corporate credit cards were built for card machines, monthly statements and companies with long credit histories. Most Indian business spending doesn't look like that. Five gaps come up again and again.


### 1. They don't work where staff actually pay


By September 2026, India had 88.5 crore UPI QR codes and 1.04 crore card machines, according to the[RBI's Payment System Indicators](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/PSIUserView.aspx?Id=64) . The gap is getting wider. In the 12 months to September 2026, UPI QR codes grew from 70.9 crore to 88.5 crore, while card machines fell from 1.21 crore to 1.04 crore. In October 2026 alone, UPI handled a record 2,547 crore payments, according to[NPCI](https://www.npci.org.in/product/upi) .


A mechanic, a tea stall, a tempo driver or a hardware shop will almost always have a QR sticker. Far fewer have a card machine.


### 2. Many businesses don't qualify


A corporate card is credit, so the bank checks the company first. One of India's largest private banks asks for at least two years in business and a minimum annual turnover of ₹10 crore. Below that, it offers corporate cards only against security such as a fixed deposit or bank guarantee. A large public sector bank draws the same ₹10 crore line.


For context, India counts a business with turnover up to ₹10 crore (and investment up to ₹2.5 crore) as a micro enterprise. So the bank's minimum sits right at the top of the micro-enterprise band.


### 3. Small vendors push back on cards


Every credit card payment costs the shop a fee, usually 1.5–2.5% of the bill. That's why so many counters say "UPI only" or add a surcharge for cards.


### 4. Control comes after the money is spent


A credit limit tells the bank how much it will lend. It doesn't tell your staff what they're allowed to buy. With cards, finance usually sees the detail when the statement arrives and the receipts are chased, weeks after the spend. By then the money has gone.


**What it looks like with a wallet:** at RDash, field teams pay site expenses from CashBook wallets and submit bills within hours of each payment, not at month end.[Read the RDash case study](https://cashbook.in/customers/rdash/)


### 5. Every card is a line of credit in the company's name


Unpaid balances attract interest, and each card adds to what the company owes. A wallet only ever holds money you've already put in.

## What are the best employee prepaid card alternatives in India?


UPI wallets are the main alternative to employee prepaid cards in India. A prepaid card fixes the credit problem but keeps the card problem. It still needs a card machine, and someone still has to print, courier and collect cards as people join and leave.


A CashBook wallet lives in the employee's CashBook app. The company keeps a master wallet and moves money from it into staff wallets. Releasing money needs an OTP sent to the person you name as Payment Admin, so money can't leave the master wallet without their sign-off.


When someone leaves, you freeze their wallet. There's no card to chase.

## How to switch your team from corporate cards to UPI wallets


1.


**Look at the last three months.** Pull card statements and expense claims. Note who spends, how often, and on what.


2.


**Start with one team.** Pick the team with the most small payments, often field sales or site staff.


3.


**Set limits from real numbers.** Base each daily limit on what that person spends on a normal day, plus some headroom.


4.


**Load wallets and explain two rules.** Pay by scanning UPI, and add the bill to every payment.


5.


**Run both for one billing cycle.** Keep the cards active for a month while the team gets used to the wallet.


6.


**Cancel the cards you no longer need.** Keep one or two for foreign travel and card-only websites.


7.


**Connect your accounts.** Sync CashBook with Tally or Zoho Books so entries reach your books without retyping.


*"Cashbook transformed how we handle small and urgent cash expenses across 9 locations, what once took days now happens in minutes"* Aditya Gupta, Executive Director,[The Raigad Group](https://cashbook.in/customers/the-raigad-group/)


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the alternatives to corporate credit cards for teams in India?


The most practical alternative is a company-funded UPI wallet, such as CashBook. Each team member pays from a wallet the company has loaded, at any of India's 88.5 crore UPI QR codes, within limits finance sets. Prepaid cards and reimbursements also replace corporate cards, but prepaid cards still need a card machine, and reimbursements make staff pay first.


### Corporate card or UPI wallet: which is better for business expenses?


For everyday business expenses in India, a UPI wallet. It works at 88.5 crore UPI QR codes against 1.04 crore card machines, spends only money you've loaded, and has the bill added to each payment. A corporate card still makes sense for foreign travel and card-only websites.

A company-funded UPI wallet. It keeps the control of a prepaid card but works wherever UPI does, and there's no physical card to print, courier or collect when someone leaves.

### What's the best alternative to expense cards for field and small teams?


A UPI wallet. Field staff pay small amounts at places that take UPI but rarely cards, and small companies often can't get a corporate card at all. When work runs over, head office can top up a CashBook wallet in seconds.


### Is a UPI wallet a good alternative to a corporate credit card?


Yes, for spending inside India. A company UPI wallet like CashBook works at any of India's 88.5 crore UPI QR codes, holds only money the company has loaded, and lets finance set limits by day, payment, payee and category. Keep a card for foreign-currency spends.

For most Indian staff spending, yes. Both are prepaid, but a prepaid card still needs one of India's 1.04 crore card machines, while a UPI wallet works at its 88.5 crore UPI QR codes. A UPI wallet also has no physical card to issue or collect.


### Can a small business get a corporate credit card in India?


Often not without security. Large banks ask for at least two years in business and ₹10 crore annual turnover. Below that, a fixed deposit or bank guarantee is usually needed. A UPI wallet like CashBook needs no credit check, because staff spend only money the company has already loaded.

Yes. Staff can scan any UPI QR code or pay a UPI ID from their CashBook wallet, within the limits you set.


### What happens to an employee's wallet when they leave?

### Does CashBook work with Tally and Zoho Books?


Yes. CashBook syncs wallet payments with Tally and Zoho Books. You can also give your accountant view-only access as an Auditor.


### Is CashBook safe for company money?


Money leaves the master wallet only after an OTP goes to your Payment Admin. Every wallet has its own limits, and any wallet can be frozen in seconds. CashBook's payments product has been reviewed by NPCI and audited by a CERT-In empanelled auditor.
